findings: limit-mem explicitly permits total process memory exceeding limit and dataset-dependent overhead. threads1 explicitly does not mean single-threaded program. Neither option proves strict resource bound.

xattr caveat explicitly acknowledges false positives when contents change without mtime change. Clamp disables cache writes; partial write-unfinished hashes are distinct from full hash-unmatched/uniques.
Cross-endian cache portability limited to endian-agnostic families; manual admits on-disk xxHash/Highway differences. Digest byte equality across architectures requires algorithm-specific tests.
mtime-window groups can chain adjacent timestamps: endpoints may differ more than configured window. This is connected-component grouping, not pairwise-diameter guarantee.
Directory equality ignores names/layout/empty content by default; honour-dir-layout changes domain. Documentation sorted-stream analogy does not prove multiplicity-sensitive implementation.
Replay claims no filesystem IO while also describing current-mtime comparison and report writes; precise interpretation is no new traversal/content hashing, not literally zero filesystem calls.
Newer-than stamp prose says updated on finish, but previously reviewed stamp writer executes at INIT. Interrupted scan cannot be treated as completed checkpoint.
Case-insensitive match is explicitly ASCII-only. Basename, dirname, relative-path and extension filters impose extra conditions beyond exact byte equality.
Manual default duplicate-size minimum1 excludes empty files, hardlink reporting and symlink policies differ from counting independent physical objects. Compare eligible domains before result totals.
Standalone equal defaults hashing and needs explicit paranoid for bytes; is-reflink has multiple nonzero states including unknown/error/inline extents. Nonzero is not universally proven not-linked.
